security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown fences, example snippets, placeholder secrets, and safety rules rather than executable behavior. No prompt injection, hidden exfiltration, or runtime command execution was found. The skill still needs content fixes because several security examples could teach weak production patterns.

remediation.issue: The CSP example allows unsafe inline scripts and styles.
remediation.suggestion: Use nonces or hashes for required inline assets, remove unsafe-inline, and document how to keep third-party origins minimal.

remediation.issue: The HTTPS redirect example trusts req.headers.host.
remediation.suggestion: Build redirects from a configured canonical hostname or a validated host allowlist, especially behind reverse proxies.

remediation.issue: The refresh token example stores bearer tokens directly.
remediation.suggestion: Store only hashed refresh tokens, rotate them on every use, and document secure transport and cookie options.

remediation.issue: Secret examples use .env-style values in the main documentation.
remediation.suggestion: Label them as placeholders or .env.example values and avoid realistic provider key prefixes where possible.

semantic_findings.title: Insecure Content Security Policy Example
semantic_findings.description: The Helmet CSP example allows unsafe inline scripts and styles while presenting itself as XSS prevention guidance. This can normalize a weak CSP that fails to block common injected inline payloads.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The unsafe-inline directives are explicit in the CSP example and appear in a section about security headers. The risk is guidance quality rather than hidden code execution.

semantic_findings.title: Host Header Trust in HTTPS Redirect
semantic_findings.description: The HTTPS redirect example constructs the redirect target from req.headers.host. If copied directly, a forged Host header can produce untrusted redirect targets or poison generated URLs.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The redirect code directly interpolates req.headers.host without a trusted host allowlist. This is a known deployment risk, although the skill only presents example code.

semantic_findings.title: Refresh Token Storage Without Hashing Guidance
semantic_findings.description: The JWT example stores refresh tokens directly in the database and rotates them by exact token value. A database leak would expose valid bearer tokens unless tokens are hashed before storage.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The example clearly persists refreshToken values and does not mention hashing or token binding. Legitimate implementations vary, so confidence is high enough for remediation but not maximal.

content.user_title: Harden Web Apps With Security Practices
content.value_statement: Web applications often ship with weak headers, unchecked inputs, and unsafe secret handling. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through practical hardening steps for APIs and infrastructure.
actual_capabilities: Recommends Express security middleware with Helmet, HSTS, and rate limiting.
Shows input validation and parameterized query patterns for injection prevention.
Provides CSRF token flow guidance for API endpoints.
Describes environment variable and Kubernetes Secret handling patterns.
Outlines JWT access token and refresh token rotation concepts.
Includes an OWASP Top 10 checklist for manual review.
limitations: Examples are templates and need framework-specific adaptation.
It does not perform automated vulnerability scanning.
It does not replace penetration testing or compliance review.
Some sample patterns should be hardened before production use.

use_cases.title: Secure a New API
use_cases.description: Add security headers, HTTPS enforcement, validation, CSRF protection, and rate limits before public launch.

use_cases.title: Review Deployment Controls
use_cases.description: Check secret handling, runtime configuration, HSTS settings, and production-safe security defaults.

use_cases.title: Run an OWASP Checklist
use_cases.description: Use the included OWASP Top 10 checklist to guide manual inspection and remediation planning.

prompt_templates.title: Add Basic Protections
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner hardening for an existing API
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to add HTTPS enforcement, security headers, and rate limiting to my web API. Explain each change in simple terms.

prompt_templates.title: Review Input Handling
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to review my API input handling for SQL injection, XSS, and unsafe validation gaps. Prioritize concrete fixes.

prompt_templates.title: Design Auth And Secrets
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design secure JWT handling, refresh token rotation, and secret storage for my production service.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Against OWASP
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to perform an OWASP Top 10 hardening review for my application. Return prioritized risks and remediation steps.

output_examples.input: Review an Express API before launch.
output: Security headers and HSTS should be enabled for production traffic.
Authentication endpoints need stricter rate limits than normal API routes.
Input validation should reject malformed data before database access.

output_examples.input: Plan secret handling for a hosted service.
output: Keep database URLs and provider keys outside source control.
Use managed secret storage or environment injection during deployment.
Rotate secrets after exposure and document ownership for each credential.
Broken access control requires route-level authorization checks.
Injection risks require parameterized database access and strict validation.
Security misconfiguration requires review of headers, CORS, and default credentials.

best_practices: Treat the examples as starting points and verify every setting against your production architecture.
Use parameterized queries, strict validation, and output encoding for all user-controlled data.
Store secrets outside source control and rotate credentials after suspected exposure.
anti_patterns: Copying placeholder secrets, domains, or policies into production without review.
Allowing inline scripts or broad origins when a strict CSP can be used.
Building redirects, CORS rules, or trust decisions from unvalidated request headers.

faq.question: Does this skill scan my code automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and review prompts for manual or AI-assisted security hardening.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. It is structured for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: Is it enough for compliance?
faq.answer: No. Use it as preparation for formal compliance, audit, and penetration testing processes.

faq.question: What frameworks does it cover?
faq.answer: The examples focus on Express, but the security principles apply to many web frameworks.

faq.question: Does it include OWASP guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes a concise OWASP Top 10 checklist for application review.

faq.question: Should I copy the examples directly?
faq.answer: No. Adapt and harden each example for your framework, hosting setup, and threat model.
